newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty down vs basket, O/N dip despite bills sale.
newsitem.headline: Zloty down vs basket, O/N dip despite bills sale.

text.p: The Polish zloty traded down against the basket of currencies after an early currency-buying impulse triggered by a small client orders pushed it to less than three percent from the central parity, dealers said.
They said that a rebuilding of currency positions by some banks that had gone short before the Christmas break might have also contibuted to a light currency-buying mood.
"The trade was weak today with currencies taken in the morning on the back of client orders or the lengthening of currency positions," said a dealer at a foreign bank in Warsaw.

The zloty closed at 2.98/2.89 percent from the trading band centre, weaker than last week's close at 3.15/3.05 percent. It closed at 2.8710/35 to the dollar, down from 2.8635/65 on Tuesday and at 1.8445/65 to the mark, down from 1.8425/45.
Overnight deposits extended fall and were offered at five percent on the overliquid market despite the sale of central bank's bills that cleared 837 million zlotys.

The NBP sold 600 million zlotys, the whole amount of 1-day NBP-bills at an average rate of 15.20 percent and the entire PLN 250 million offer of 91-day bills at an average rate of 21.85 percent, 0.18 point higher than the previous rate.
Overnight deposits were quoted at 2.00/5.00 percent, down from opening's 15 pct at offer.

The NBP also drained 178 million zlotys off the market for 14 days at an unchanged maximum rate of 21.64 percent. Despite that tomorrow/next deposits fell to 20.50/21.95 percent from 21.00/22.00 percent at 0930 GMT.

Minimum prices of all Polish T-bills fell at today's primary auction on total demand of 423 million zlotys against a 900 million zloty offer. The ministry sold a total of 358 million zlotys worth of T-bills.
